news.title: Junior Bula Boys ready for FIFA U20 World Cup qualification bid
news.lede: The Junior Bula Boys are ready to step onto the international stage and represent Fiji at the OFC U19 Men’s Championship in Samoa. The young players have been told to embrace the pressure and responsibility that comes with wearing the national jersey as they prepare to take on the region’s best in their bid to qualify for the FIFA U20 World Cup. Fiji U19 Men’s National Team Head of Delegation Surend Prasad says the team is prepared for the challenge and believes the players have what it takes to represent the country with pride. Speaking during the team’s official presentation and jersey handover, Prasad says the Junior Bula Boys understand that the road ahead will not be easy, with pressure, challenges and difficult matches expected.

news.title: Nigeria Football Leadership Rocked by Mass Resignation after World Cup Failures
news.lede: By Boris Esono Nwenfor BUEA, PAV – Nigeria’s football leadership has been thrown into turmoil after the president of the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Ibrahim Musa Gusau, the general secretary, Mohammed Sanusi, and the federation’s entire executive committee resigned weeks before scheduled elections. The NFF confirmed the departures on Thursday, August 27, 2026, saying they followed growing public dissatisfaction with the recent performances of the country's national teams. Ibrahim Gusau said his decision to resign was intended to create room for wider reforms within Nigerian football. The leadership crisis follows the Super Eagles’ failure to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the Super Falcons’ failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil.

news.title: Liverpool are overpaying for Bradley Barcola - but joining the Reds offers flying Frenchman the chance to become a global superstar: GOAL grades the biggest deals of the 2026 summer transfer windowl
news.lede: For some football fans, the summer is the part of the calendar that they look forward to the most - and that's not just because it's filled by a World Cup every four years! Rather, it's because the end of the season means only one thing: It's time for transfers! The 2026 window is once again proving to be busy, with some huge names making big-money moves before deadline day on September 1. We know that some transfers turn out well for all parties involved, but there are plenty where at least one of the clubs, or even the player, are left wondering what might have been had they made a different decision while at the negotiating table.

news.title: FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027: A New Chapter
news.lede: The countdown to the FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027 has officially begun. For the first time in history, the tournament will be hosted in South America, with Brazil welcoming the world’s biggest women’s football event. In this special monthly series, we will bring you the latest updates, behind-the-scenes stories and insights from professionals and key figures in the game, through the perspective of our exclusive correspondent in Brazil, Elena Mueller. The FIFA Women’s World Cup Brazil 2027 will take place from 24 June to 25 July 2027 across eight host cities: Belo Horizonte, Brasília, Fortaleza, Porto Alegre, Recife, Rio de Janeiro, Salvador and São Paulo.
